In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a cyclostationarity-based channel estimation scheme for the identification and equalization problem, where the input sequence is generated by a periodic precoder.
the development of blind identification and equalizing techniques for cyclostationary channels induced by the periodic modulation of the input symbol stream.

the design and analysis of cyclostationarity inducing transmitters and receivers, with the purpose of exploiting cyclostationarity at the transmitter and receiver sides to improve channel estimation, equalization and detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MIC-based systems present a tradeoff between channel estimation and equalization performance.

cyclostationarity-based transmitters provide a better channel estimation capability at a cost of a slightly higher MMSE/BER in the equalization process, and thus, they represent a viable alternative for future communications systems.
cyclostationarity inducing modulation is a very promising technique for channel estimation, but its use for equalization is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, although the proposed MIC framework does not provide any advantage in the equalization stage, it is very useful for channel estimation purposes, especially when channel identification is performed in a blind fashion.
cyclostationarity inducing precoding is a promising technique for channel estimation, but it is not necessarily the best option for channel equalization.
, although MIC-based systems present a number of interesting advantages relative to the stationary case, they are not a panacea for all channel equalization problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyclostationarities induced by the periodic modulation precoder are not sufficient to provide a substantial improvement in the performance of MMSE equalizers.
MIC-based systems can achieve a significant reduction in training overhead and complexity, while providing performance that is close to their stationary counterparts.
MIC-based transmitters are a viable alternative for channel identification in the presence of additive noise.
